This layer plugs Supabase sign-in into the admin shell of `@plutocms/pluto`. Core owns the `/admin` route, the sign-in page, the route guard, and the navbar. This layer registers an `authDriver` and a few other registry entries. See [Admin shell](/core/admin-shell).

## The driver

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `user()` | The Supabase user mapped from the JWT claims. The id is `sub`. The name is `display_name`, then `full_name`, then `name`, from `user_metadata`. |
| `loggedIn()` | `true` when a Supabase session exists. The session cookie gives the same answer on the server and in the first client render, so there is no hydration mismatch. |
| `ready()` | Resolves at once. The module plugin of `@nuxtjs/supabase` reads the session first. |
| `refresh()` | Reads the session and the claims again. |
| `signOut()` | Calls `supabase.auth.signOut()` and clears the session state. |
| `signIn` | The email and password form `AuthSignIn`. It opens `redirect`, else `/admin/home`. |
| `guard(to)` | The setup guard. |
| `links` | Sign up and forgot password. |
| `publicPaths` | See the next section. |

## Public paths

| Path | A signed-in user |
| --- | --- |
| `/admin/signup` | Goes to the admin home |
| `/admin/forgot-password` | Goes to the admin home |
| `/admin/confirm` | Stays on the page. A confirm link signs the user in. |
| `/admin/update-password` | Stays on the page. A recovery link signs the user in. |
| `/admin/accept-invite` | Stays on the page. An invite link signs the user in. |
| `/admin/setup` | Stays on the page. The setup guard decides. |

The sign-up, forgot-password, update-password, and confirm pages use `PlutoAdminAuthCard` with the `auth` layout. Every auth page has the same frame as the sign-in page.

## Accepting an invite

The page `/admin/accept-invite` is behind the invite email. The browser client uses PKCE. The default invite email gives tokens in the URL hash, which the PKCE client does not read. So the page reads the link itself.

| Link | What the page does |
| --- | --- |
| `?token_hash=...&type=invite` | Verifies the one-time code as an invite |
| `?token_hash=...&type=magiclink` (or `signup`) | Verifies the one-time code as a magic link |
| `#access_token=...&refresh_token=...` | Sets the session from the tokens |
| `#error_code=otp_expired` (or any `error_code`) | Shows "Link expired, ask for a new invite" |
| No token, but a session | Goes on to the password form |
| Nothing | Shows "Invalid link" |

The page clears the URL. Then it shows a password form with a confirm field. It updates the password, refreshes the driver, and goes to `/admin/home`.

## The setup guard

The driver `guard(to)` runs on `/admin/**`, after `ready()` and before the sign-in rule. A new install goes to `/admin/setup` and not to the sign-in page.

- Setup not done, or the state cannot be read: every admin path but `/admin/setup` goes to `/admin/setup`.
- Setup done: `/admin/setup` goes to `/admin/login`.

::warning
Keep the second rule. The setup page asks an anonymous visitor for a database connection string. It is safe only because it is unreachable after the setup.
::

A finished setup is cached, so the guard does not fetch on every navigation. A result that is not "done" is read again each time. The guard never rejects.

## Site info

`site.name()` is the `website_title` setting. `site.url()` is the `website_url` setting. In development, `url()` is empty, so **View site** opens `/`.

## Banner

The migrations banner is in `adminBanners`. Core's admin layout renders it. It hides on `/admin/migrations`.

## Permissions and language

This layer has no sync plugin. The core plugin `pluto-auth-sync.client.ts` watches `loggedIn`. It loads the capabilities and the stored language after sign-in, and clears the capabilities after sign-out.

## `useAuth()`

`useAuth()` has `login`, `requestPasswordReset`, and `updatePassword`. Use `usePlutoAuth()` from core for the user and the sign-out.

The sign-up page posts to `POST /api/auth/signup`. The body has `username` (3 characters or more), `display_name`, `email`, and `password` (6 characters or more).

## Migrate an older app

Before version 0.11, this layer had its own navbar, its own `pages/admin.vue`, its own sign-in page, and its own `auth` middleware. They are gone.

- If you overrode `NavbarAdmin` or `NavbarAdminProvider`, delete the override. Add a link action to `navbarActions`, an item to `accountMenu`, or a banner to `adminBanners`.
- If you overrode `pages/admin.vue`, delete the override. Move extra work to a banner or a plugin.
- If you overrode `pages/admin/(auth)/login.vue`, delete it. Register another `signIn` component in an `authDriver`.
- If you used the `auth` route middleware by name, remove the name.
- `useAuth()` no longer returns `isLoggedIn`, `user`, `logout`, or `allowedUnauthenticatedPaths`. Use `usePlutoAuth()`.
- The `supabase.navbar.*` keys are removed. Core has `pluto.navbar.*`.
- The layer depends on `@plutocms/pluto` 0.18 or later. The layer installs it for you. Do not add it to your app.

The old `admin.vue` showed a "not logged in" toast when the browser tab became visible with no session. Core's guard runs on navigation only, so this toast is gone.
